sections.heading: Sets and functions
paragraphs: A set contains distinct elements; a subset contains only elements of its reference set, and disjoint sets share no elements. Union includes either set, intersection includes both, A−B includes elements only in A, and A’s complement contains the elements of the universal set outside A.

A function maps each domain element to exactly one codomain element. Its range is the set actually reached; onto means the range equals the codomain, and one-to-one means distinct inputs have distinct outputs. A function has an inverse on its full codomain when it is both one-to-one and onto. For f(x)=mx+b on the reals with m≠0, f⁻¹(y)=(y−b)/m.

sections.heading: Probability and random variables
paragraphs: A probability space consists of sample space S, an event σ-algebra, and probability measure P. Events are measurable subsets of S; P(S)=1, and probabilities of disjoint events add. A σ-algebra includes S and is closed under complements and countable unions. Page 15’s claim that any σ-algebra on k outcomes has 2^k events is too broad: this count applies to the full power set.
For the three-sided die, P(B)=1/6, P(C)=1/3 and P(D)=1/2; therefore P(B or C)=1/2 and P(C or D)=5/6. The full event collection has 2³=8 events.

A random variable assigns real numbers to outcomes. Its cumulative distribution F(x)=P(X≤x) is nondecreasing, and P(a<X≤b)=F(b)−F(a). For a continuous distribution with density f, interval probabilities are areas under f, and F(x) is the integral of f up to x.

sections.heading: Distributions and random variates
paragraphs: Uniform(a,b) has constant density over its interval; triangular(a,m,b) is useful when minimum, most likely value, and maximum are known but the exact shape is not. Exponential interarrival times have mean m and rate λ=1/m; for x≥0, P(X>x)=exp(−λx). Normal(m,σ) describes variability around a mean, with σ the standard deviation.

Page 25’s displayed exponential density omits the rate multiplier: the normalized density is λ exp(−λx) for x≥0. A continuous uniform distribution gives equal probabilities to equal-length intervals, not a positive equal probability to each individual real value.

Simulation first generates a uniform random number and transforms it into a random variate with the desired distribution. A linear congruential generator uses Zₖ₊₁=(aZₖ+c) mod m and Uₖ=Zₖ/m; its integers repeat after a period no longer than m. For a full cycle, c and m must be relatively prime; every prime factor of m divides a−1; and if 4 divides m, then 4 divides a−1.

sections.heading: Input and output modeling
paragraphs: Structural modeling identifies entities, locations, resources and processes; data modeling supplies quantitative inputs such as interarrival times, service times, schedules, failures and travel times.

Direct sample use preserves recorded values but limited samples may miss rare possibilities and repeated retrieval can be costly. An empirical distribution represents observed samples and can generate arbitrarily long streams, but cannot produce unobserved outliers. A fitted theoretical distribution can smooth sample irregularities, but fitting takes effort and a good fit may not exist. Complex input-data cases include no data, multimodal, correlated, and nonstationary data.

Output data analysis converts simulation output into information about system performance; the slides introduce the confidence interval for a mean and identify more complex analysis situations without giving a detailed procedure.

sections.heading: DES elements and clock advance
paragraphs: Discrete-event simulation represents a system whose modeled state changes at separated event times. The module describes its DES examples as stochastic and dynamic; stochasticity is not inherent to every possible DES model. An entity moves through the system, attributes carry entity-specific information, resources provide service, and queues hold entities waiting for occupied resources. An event changes system state.

Resource capacity is the number served simultaneously; utilization is busy time divided by total observed time. The simulation executive controls clock advance and event execution. A next-event list holds scheduled event times; timing selects the next event, the event routine updates state, accumulators gather performance information, and the report generator summarizes results.

Fixed-increment advancement updates at chosen time steps and can force between-step events onto a boundary. Next-event advancement moves directly to the earliest scheduled event, updates state there, and skips inactive intervals. The simulation clock represents elapsed simulated time, not necessarily elapsed wall-clock time.

sections.heading: Queue behavior and worked example
paragraphs: A queueing model describes arrivals, service and the rule for selecting waiting customers. Variation in arrival and service times can cause waiting. FCFS/FIFO serves the earliest arrival first; LIFO/LCFS serves the most recent first; priority and shortest-processing-time rules select differently. Page 66 mistakenly labels last-in-first-out as FIFO; it should be LIFO.

Balking means deciding not to enter a line, reneging means leaving after joining but before service, and jockeying means switching lines. A design may balance the cost of service capacity against the cost of waiting. Systems may have single or multiple servers and single or multiple service phases.

For the page 78–79 single-server FCFS example, arrivals are 0,4,5,9,11,15 and service times are 2,3,1,4,2,3. Service starts at 0,4,7,9,13,15 and ends at 2,7,8,13,15,18. Waits are 0,0,2,0,2,0; total wait is 4 and mean wait is 4/6. Customer 5 spends 15−11=4 time units in the system.

For an initially idle single server, startᵢ=max(arrivalᵢ, endᵢ₋₁), waitᵢ=startᵢ−arrivalᵢ, endᵢ=startᵢ+serviceᵢ, and time in system=endᵢ−arrivalᵢ. Idle time before a customer is max(0, arrivalᵢ−endᵢ₋₁). Page 77 reverses the waiting-time subtraction and incorrectly says the first service always begins at zero; it begins at the first arrival when the initially idle server is available. Its interarrival indexing is also inconsistent.
